text: Why were people in China swallowing their own history?
For centuries, farmers near Anyang dug up strange old bones.
Medicine shops ground these dragon bones into powder... and people swallowed it.
Some had odd scratches, so the farmers scraped them clean first.
Then, in eighteen ninety-nine, a Beijing scholar named Wang Yirong looked closer.
Those scratches were writing. Over three thousand years old.
Shang kings had carved questions into turtle shells and ox bones.
Will it rain? Will we win? Is a dead ancestor causing my toothache?
Then a diviner pushed fire into the bone... and read the cracks.
Legend says Wang found them in his malaria medicine.
More likely, an antiques dealer sold them to him.
Since then, over a hundred thousand pieces have surfaced.
And many of those symbols still live inside Chinese characters today.
China's oldest library was almost eaten, one spoonful at a time.
History's biggest clues often hide in what we call junk.
If you could ask the bones one question, what would it be?
